People call methadone a life sentence, a ball and chain. In a new Cato Podcast episode, @dr4liberty talks with Helen Redmond, author of “Liquid Handcuffs,” about how a Nixon-era crime control program became America’s dominant addiction treatment model, and why people with addiction should be able to access methadone directly from health care providers.

Listen on Apple, Spotify, and our website!
 
Apple: ow.ly/UIhS50YVISp 
Spotify: ow.ly/cOVU50YVISs 
Our website: ow.ly/tyvi50YVISJ

As America turns 250, “Proclaiming Liberty” by @TimothySandefur revisits the revolutionary year of 1776 through the minds of John Adams and Thomas Jefferson. 
  
The ideal read before July 4th. Order your copy today! 
cato.org/books/proclaiming-l…

The Trump administration reportedly is considering vetting AI tools before they are released. This precautionary approach threatens free expression just as it did when the Biden administration took this path, says Cato’s @dr_inserra.

Federal power is enumerated, not unlimited. Yet prosecutors tried to stretch a stadium flare incident into a 7-year federal “arson” charge—until a judge pushed back. Cato’s @foxmike90 argues an ever-expanding view of federal authority undermines federalism. 

ow.ly/NuGQ50YVfTI

Friends of the Cato Institute came out in force for the Cato on Tour event at the Harvard Club. 

If you weren't there, you missed a timely dialogue with Cato's @ConLawWarrior, @David_J_Bier, Harrison Moar, @johanknorberg, and President Peter Goettler about how executive power is expanding—and how we can defend liberty. 

To get up to speed, check out our Vision for Liberty Campaign: ow.ly/nCa750YVB0U

Thank you to everyone who joined us. We'll be back in NYC in the fall with more.

Caption for X: The CFPB promises to follow the law and cut overregulation, but the agency was built for overreach. Only Congress can make lasting reforms.

The SEC’s “Gag Rule” forces people who settle cases to stay silent forever—even if the agency is wrong. That’s not a free choice; it’s pressure. Critics say it violates free speech and want the Supreme Court to strike it down.

ow.ly/Zsxt50YVf3I

Join us for a conversation with leading European voices on the future of digital taxation. 

Featuring: Cato’s @adamnmichel, @ahellmanndc of the Tholos Foundation, @crisberechet of Tax Foundation Europe, and @MatBauerEcon of the European Centre for International Political Economy.
nitter.net/i/broadcasts/1YxNrZqkP…

Regulators label certain banks “too big to fail,” then add an extra safety cushion requirement as if it fixes the underlying problem. Cato’s @norbertjmichel argues the framework punishes scale and misses the real risks.

ow.ly/aqt150YVawf

Your Social Security contributions aren't saved for you — they're paying today's retirees. 

It's a transfer system, not a savings program. And the math no longer adds up. Cato's @RominaBoccia explains.

Video

“Proclaiming Liberty” by @TimothySandefur is a fast-paced intellectual history that traces how John Adams, Thomas Jefferson, and their contemporaries transformed centuries of political thought into the revolutionary principles of the Declaration of Independence—and why those principles still matter today.

When assigned schools fail don’t work for students, schools like Oakmont's career-focused charters can be the difference between dropping out and building a life.

ow.ly/9Oy150YV9Li

FBI Director Patel's defamation suit against The Atlantic will likely fail. That demonstrates two problems. The law not only fails to deter powerful people from filing baseless defamation suits but also fails to protect those who have actually been defamed, explains Cato's Dan Greenberg.
ow.ly/7X7750YV9kI

It’s Teacher Appreciation Week! 

The best way to appreciate teachers is educational freedom. School choice opens new options for teachers, not just students, Cato's @ColleenHroncich explains. 

ow.ly/QF4W50YV9Hb

SCOTUS just rewrote the rules on voting maps in Louisiana v. Callais: race can’t drive districting, and plaintiffs must prove intentional discrimination—not just unequal outcomes. Critics warn it weakens minority protections; supporters say it curbs racial overreach. Cato’s Robert Levy explains.

ow.ly/HBei50YV7C9

The psychiatric system makes you get a diagnosis for drugs millions already use—then makes it hard to stop. People deserve better, say Cato’s @dr4liberty  and @AdamOmaryPhD.

ow.ly/W61Y50YV4Xy
